body:
# T288 candidate — protected local channel lifecycle and receive events

Provisional ID; independent P1 required before rails/source. Supersedes the separate-input candidate, archived separately. No inventory prerequisite is proposed. The premise review is correct: a physical tier is not necessary when the existing primary has a mandatory local-only ingress boundary. This ticket adds real channel-service participation, not an unused receipt service. No renderer activation, serving, tool discovery or new storage tier.

## Trust/bootstrap contract

Supported operation is one trusted writing Gateway per store, initialized from an existing backend that has NEVER accepted this NEW vocabulary through generic import, or reopened/restored from a complete history produced under this ticket's guarded writer discipline. Raw backend/reactor writes are trusted host capabilities. Arbitrary prepopulated same-key local-event rows are NOT distinguishable from legitimate history on Gateway.open; signatures/version markers cannot establish that provenance. Hosts must not feed such content into the trusted reopen path and call it ordinary federation.

A whole-home restore preserving local events is restoration of the SAME logical authority history, including opening incarnations; a new independent home starts without those local events and imports content only through guarded federation. No automatic sanitization or claim that boot detects a dishonest restore. This is an explicit precondition comparable to existing trusted backend wiring, not a secret authority flag. No separate bootstrap boolean/index is introduced.

Upgrade behavior: legacy channels continue their existing root/operator open/resume/sync/renderer behavior but have NO authoritative protected incarnation/received set. Resume must not silently mint protected evidence from old controls/arrival stamps. A deliberate fresh open after successful ordinary drop gets a protected incarnation. Automatic in-place promotion of an old channel is out of scope. New fresh local opens (root or bound) create protected events, but only later activation code will use them. Imported legacy controls can still drive legacy behavior as today; they cannot create protected custody.

## Source files / scope

- New `src/federation/local-channel-events.ts`: strict event claims/parser/projector, narrow service writer, shared channel queue helper.
- `src/federation/channel.ts`: fresh open event, close retirement, sync received-result attestation, fresh/resumed handles share queue, protected reader uses exact attachment/opening association.
- `src/gateway/ingest.ts`: non-overridable generic local-family rejection; private/narrow validated persistence seam for service; opt-in admitted-offer ID reporting from actual ingest decisions.
- `src/gateway/gateway.ts`: optional report type addition and host-owned queue state (ordering only); internal service capability wiring if needed.
- `src/gateway/erase.ts`: narrow trusted-local event-erasure persistence and control provenance described below; no extra purge target/tier.
- New `test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts`; relevant existing ingress/channel lifecycle/arrival/erasure compatibility suites as controls. No canonical tests changed without gate process.

## API for independent rails

```ts
export interface LocalChannelOpening {
  readonly id: string; // protected open delta ID; full incarnation
  readonly channel: string;
  readonly into: string;
  readonly prefix: string;
  readonly from: string;
  readonly openedBy?: string;
  readonly openedFrom?: string;
  readonly statusAtOpen: string; // exact legacy channel-status delta ref
  readonly poolDeclaration: string; // exact attached channel-container declaration ref
}
export type LocalChannelEvidence =
 | { readonly state: "legacy" }
 | { readonly state: "closed"; readonly opening: LocalChannelOpening }
 | { readonly state: "unavailable"; readonly reason: string }
 | { readonly state: "open"; readonly opening: LocalChannelOpening;
     readonly received: readonly Delta[] };
export function localChannelEvidence(gw: Gateway, channel: string): LocalChannelEvidence;
export function withChannelCommit<T>(
  gw: Gateway, channel: string, body: () => Promise<T>,
): Promise<T>;
```

These are internal exports; `withChannelCommit` is a trusted host coordination capability, not transport input. No exported `record(receipts)` taking arbitrary remote claims. The channel service's writer constructs/signs its own events using its existing explicit operated-gateway capability. The ingestion bypass is module-private/capability-scoped and not an `allowLocal:true` option on Gateway.append/federate. Factor shared validation/persist logic if necessary so bypass does not skip signature, tombstone or cite-slate rules.

Optional federation result: `federate(deltas, { ids: true, admittedIds: true })` returns `admittedIds: readonly string[]` in addition to existing counts/acceptedIds. `admittedIds:true` requires `ids:true` (reject the other combination). These are unique sorted IDs that passed validation/admission/closure, whose backend write succeeded, and whose actual ingest was accepted or whose non-accepted outcome is independently confirmed against an existing identical verified delta (compare complete signed delta, not ID alone). An explicit rejected ingest is excluded even if a later lookup finds bytes; an exception/partial exceptional ingest rejects the operation and returns no successful attestation result. Return only after this actual ingest pass completes; never return the preselection array. Existing calls/report shape remain unchanged unless requested. Neither offered IDs nor pooled presence substitutes for this result. Parser reserve checks happen before arbitrary admit predicate and before batch closure; excluded protected events cannot be readmitted by closure.

## Exact v1 pointer vocabulary

Single reserved context `loam.local.channel.event`; all event claims use receiver operator author, finite nonnegative integer timestamp, strict order/cardinality, no unknown pointers. The first pointer is:

`{"role":"event","target":{"kind":"entity","entity":{"id":"channel:NAME","context":"loam.local.channel.event"}}}`

followed by primitive `version:1` and primitive `action` (`open`, `received`, `close`). NAME is exact existing channel name, nonempty/NUL-free. Fresh opening includes 32 random bytes as lowercase hex `nonce`, ensuring a new full delta ID even if timestamp/fields repeat. Nonce is uniqueness, not authority evidence.

**Open** remaining pointers, in order: primitive `nonce`; primitive `into`; primitive `prefix`; primitive `from`; primitive `opener-kind`=`root` or `bound`; bound only primitives `opened-by`, `opened-from`; delta-kind `status-at-open`; delta-kind `pool-declaration`. Root has neither bound pointer; half-bound shape refuses. Strings preserve actual channel values; channel/into/prefix and bound attribution are nonempty, while from may be empty for an explicitly local/nonnetwork source. Reference IDs must be full valid delta addresses. Referenced status and pool declaration must exist at issuance and agree with all recorded fields.

**Received** remaining pointers: delta-kind `opening`, then one or more delta-kind `received`, unique and lexicographically sorted. Record all validated/admitted IDs from the actual event, including source-author retractions and their accepted forward negation closure; no renderer-only filter. Deduplicate against IDs in currently effective held received events under this exact opening to avoid poll churn. A held-but-never-attested source gets its first honest receipt only when it is actually offered/validated/admitted again. A later new strike receives a new event. Receipt timestamp is this receive event, never an invented old arrival time.

**Close** remaining pointers: delta-kind `opening`; primitive `reason`=`drop`. An effective held close retires that opening until explicit trusted-local erasure changes the evidence. Imported negations cannot lift it. Explicit fresh reopening creates a new full opening ID.

Literal claims fixture, with A/B replaced by real full signed fixture IDs:

```json
{"timestamp":101,"author":"OP","pointers":[
 {"role":"event","target":{"kind":"entity","entity":{"id":"channel:channel:ada:journal:peer","context":"loam.local.channel.event"}}},
 {"role":"version","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":1}},
 {"role":"action","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"received"}},
 {"role":"opening","target":{"kind":"delta","deltaRef":{"delta":"A"}}},
 {"role":"received","target":{"kind":"delta","deltaRef":{"delta":"B"}}}
]}
```

Raw literal negative fixtures must exercise wrong pointer kind, partial bound opener, duplicate refs, mismatched channel/opening, short IDs and extra roles without relying on production builders.

## Generic ingress and negations

Gateway.append rejects ANY delta with ANY entity pointer in the reserved context, even wrong role/malformed payload and even operator-signed. Federation rejects it unconditionally, including admit override and seeded-root input. Generic append/federate also reject negations that target protected event IDs already held or included in the offered batch. Unknown-target negations may remain ordinary data for legacy compatibility, but the protected projector NEVER uses generic negation algebra to determine open/close/receipt standing: only locally issued typed close retires an open. Thus preplanted unknown-target strikes, later negation-of-negation and same-key imported controls cannot change this event history. Invalid/foreign-author reserved events present through a trusted corrupted restore make evidence unavailable, not a valid local act.

Direct backend/reactor mutation and intentional raw restore remain trusted host paths; tools/HTTP raw append and ordinary federation are not trusted and must hit these guards. Test both library ingress and actual raw append HTTP control for the reserved family. Existing arbitrary ordinary data/signatures remain governed as before.

## Lifecycle, source closure and commit queue

Use one root-owned rejection-safe Promise tail per channel NAME so old/new handles and reopen operations coordinate, not only per transient handle/incarnation. Queue is synchronization only; replay authority is deltas. Fresh open, drop and receive commit acquire it. Fresh/resumed handle sync calls must share it; keepSyncing's current scheduler-local chain is insufficient. Network pull can happen outside the queue; revalidate current legacy status, protected opening, scope/source and attachment at queue entry. No stale pulled offer may commit into a replaced opening. Record channel handle's exact incarnation when created/resumed.

Fresh open: preserve existing validation/pool creation and legacy status persistence; then issue protected open referencing those exact deltas before returning a protected handle. If protected event append fails, report failure; legacy channel/pool may remain as unprotected state. Do not pretend rollback occurred or auto-adopt that partial state on resume.

Receive inside queue: validate association -> pool.federate with admittedIds -> protected received event primary append -> finish existing bookkeeping. Existing legacy arrivalClaims/debt remain compatibility evidence only; NEVER use their owed IDs as protected custody. Source append before receipt crash leaves held unproven bytes. Next genuine offer can validate already-held IDs and attest them then. Empty/unchanged already-attested offers add no protected event.

Projection received operand is union of refs in protected received events for the exact current open, resolved from its exact pool. It includes positive source deltas AND received negation lineage. Root-seeded/raw pool facts and strikes outside this received set do not alter this lineage. A received source-author retraction retires that source; negation-of-negation follows existing source-author survival over the complete received operand. Newer unstruck route winner is separate source selection, never automatic substitution. Missing referenced source bytes makes evidence unavailable for that source, never recreates bytes.

Drop: after the existing cheap legitimacy/real-backend checks but BEFORE destructive pool.drop, append protected close inside queue. A later purge failure leaves legacy pool attached as today but its protected opening closed; report that partial outcome. Retry drop may finish legacy cleanup. Reopen requires old drop completed and creates a new open. Resume reuses current protected open only if exact source/opener/pool declaration agree with attached legacy state; otherwise evidence unavailable/legacy, no remint.

| Outcome | Protected evidence | Legacy behavior |
|---|---|---|
| old channel resumes | legacy | unchanged sync/operator apps |
| fresh open succeeds | open, exact new ID | existing status/pool |
| open event append fails | legacy/unavailable | possible partial channel retained, caller gets failure |
| source commit succeeds, receipt fails/crash | newly held IDs unproven | bytes held; sync failure/debt behavior retained |
| receipt succeeds | exact received operand grows | ordinary sync continues |
| close succeeds, pool purge fails | closed | existing partial-drop failure/held bytes |
| normal resume | same opening/received refs | no protected churn |
| same name reopened | new opening, old refs excluded | existing fresh channel semantics |

## Explicit trusted-local erasure; generic deletion controls

Permit `Gateway.erase(eventId)` with its ordinary operated-host authority. This is a trusted local API, not permission for an operator-signed wire payload to enter via generic append. Persist the normal valid tombstone via a narrow internal capability shared with erasure, preserving eraseDefect, cite, budget/signature validation and persist-before-observe. No public allowLocal option.

For erasure of a protected event, add a reserved provenance marker to the ordinary tombstone: entity pointer role `local-control` at context `loam.local.channel.control`, entity ID equal to the exact event delta ID; primitive `local-control-version:1`; primitive `local-control-kind:"erase"`. The existing ordinary `erases`, `spoken-by`, reason/slate and tombstone marker pointers retain their normal schema. Strict local parser requires one provenance marker and exact equality of marker ID and erases ref. This explicit delta evidence preserves protected-target identification AFTER original event bytes are purged; it is not a hidden target index. Generic ingress excludes this second reserved context as unconditionally as positive events. The marker is attribution of a local operation only because of the sole writer boundary, not its signature.

A single generic guard, run before callbacks and closure, rejects positive events and reserved local controls, plus any negation/erasure targeting held or batch-proposed protected events or reserved control records, recursively through forward negation closure. Receipt erasure tombstones remain protected subjects after their event disappears. Generic controls must never become local event forgiveness. Unknown-target controls can remain inert ordinary data; the event writer checks effective tombstones before issuance and refuses a precondemned ID. The protected projection ignores arbitrary generic event negations and accepts event deletion authority only through validated locally marked tombstones. A preplanted unknown-target control cannot later acquire protected meaning merely when its target is minted.

Explicit intermediate limitation: T288 introduces NO local-forgiveness API for protected event erasures. Generic forgiveness/negation-of-negation over protected controls refuses. Ordinary data forgiveness stays unchanged; this candidate does not claim complete protected-event forgiveness support. Add a narrow typed local forgiveness capability in a later ticket if needed, rather than exposing a raw-signature bypass now. Supported trusted reopen must preserve this v1 history; a history containing unsupported protected-control variants yields unavailable evidence. This limitation must be accepted at P1 but needs no invented append-only event restriction.

Exposed `eraseReplica` must not serve as a second minting path: event-targeted erasure there requires a validated marked local tombstone already held at the attached host authority (same exact signed delta), via legitimate host fan-out. An unattached/direct caller cannot manufacture authority by handing it a fresh same-key tombstone. Ordinary source/data replica erasure remains unchanged. Existing pre-open restore/heal may finish a genuine supported local erasure from its ordinary tombstone; no CLI changes or blanket conflict refusal.

Projector uses effective local tombstones even if purge failed and event bytes remain. Erase(open) removes the necessary incarnation. Erase(received) removes its operand contribution; erasing a received-strike event may expose earlier source support under deliberate ordinary erasure semantics. Erase(close) may revive only an otherwise valid exact currently attached opening; never reattach a dropped pool, remint an opening or substitute a source. Source erasure remains ordinary exact-ID erasure and leaves primary receipt citations dangling. No new physical tier, global inventory, cascade or purge target set.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Same-key A/B homes: ordinary append, federation override and root seeding cannot import A's protected open/received/close as B's local events; imported legacy controls/unknown strikes cannot manufacture or revive them. Ordinary legacy root channel controls still function. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
2. Real fresh bound/root channel open, received fact, close and reopen produce exact literal-schema events with source/opening/inbox/pool refs. Resume preserves ID; legacy resume never upgrades itself. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
3. Actual held source offered again yields first protected receipt; pooled-only source, old arrival stamp and unattested debt do not. Signature/admission-refused offered IDs never receive attestation. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
4. Received source-author strike and strike-of-strike are included and projected correctly; unreceived root-seeded/raw strikes do not decide received lineage. Real source erasure yields unavailable source and reported dangling citation. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
5. Delaying source/primary backends prove source-before-receipt crash fail-closed and retry after actual offer; no fictional atomic cross-backend transaction. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
6. Two handles plus scheduler/manual sync and drop/reopen share commit order. Hold commit, race stale offer/drop; no event lands for wrong incarnation. Queue failure does not poison later calls. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
7. Open-event failure and close-before-purge failure have the exact partial outcomes in table; existing independent operator app/legacy channel behavior otherwise passes original rails. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
8. Trusted-local event erasure succeeds with exact-ID/bystander semantics; same-key generic deletion and forgiveness controls refuse, including after original event bytes disappear. Direct unattached replica calls cannot mint local deletion. Supported pending-erasure restore remains valid. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.
9. Restart from supported durable history reproduces evidence exclusively from deltas. Explicitly document/test ordinary content import versus trusted whole-history restore; do not claim same-key arbitrary prepopulation is detectable. Verify: test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts with the real-state and failure-seam controls specified below.

## Remaining P1 checks

No product permission question remains. Recheck executability of the explicitly unsupported protected-event forgiveness limitation and strict local-control marker schema. The trusted upgrade/restore precondition is retained: arbitrary prepopulated same-key events cannot be recognized as local by replay. No CLI recovery changes, inventory prerequisite or physical tier are needed. Root should freeze only after independent review accepts the complete revised contract.

## Final queue and exact-reference rules (normative)

Public `openChannelImpl`, returned `channel.sync`, and `dropChannelImpl` are queued wrappers around private already-in-commit helpers. `withChannelCommit` is non-reentrant; a caller holding it must use private helpers, never reenter a public wrapper. Protected writer, stamp and legacy status cleanup inside these helpers do not acquire it again. Future activation must similarly call its private commit body inside the shared queue. Per-name queues do not promise new cross-name prefix-collision atomicity.

`stamp` returns the exact Delta it persisted. Fresh pool creation must expose/capture the exact newly authored channel-container declaration Delta through an internal creation result; add `src/gateway/container.ts` to scope for this result if required. Do not recover either ID by scanning latest rows after awaits. The creation result distinguishes freshly minted declaration/pool versus existing attached/unresumed handle and partial failed opening. Only a truly new lifecycle (new declaration, no surviving prior pool lifecycle) gets protected open. Missing federationChannels handle is insufficient. Existing handle reuse, resume, and partial open retry never mint a protected opening automatically.

Every post-pull path enters the same queued commit helper, including pull REJECTION, optimistic debt, success/failure status stamp and received-event write. Re-read current legacy fields inside commit. Captured handle incarnation, source/opener/into/prefix and exact pool declaration must still agree. Stale successful OR failed pull rejects `stale channel operation` WITHOUT any debt/status/receipt write. Do not let an old network failure overwrite a fresh reopen. Legacy handles without protected evidence still compare their captured exact legacy lifecycle/attachment association so they cannot overwrite a replacement.

Drop holds the queue through protected close, pool.drop, maps and legacy status strikes. It must never await scheduler.stop while holding the queue, because stop waits for queued sync. Stop scheduling outside this critical section; queued stale sync settles by association refusal. A failed close append prevents pool.drop. A successful close followed by failed pool.drop leaves protected evidence closed until explicit erase(close) or later completed drop/new open. Retry does not append redundant closes.

Historical `statusAtOpen`: exact delta must be held, parse correctly and agree with original open fields; it need NOT remain latest or unnegated merely because later ordinary status stamps exist. It must not be effectively erased. Pool declaration reference: exact delta must be held, parse correctly, survive current lawful declaration selection and identify the CURRENT attached pool's declaration, not merely an identical name. Fresh drop/reopen must mint a different exact declaration; failed drop leaves the old declaration if still current. If current identity cannot be recovered unambiguously from existing container APIs, return unavailable; never use a name as substitute.

Malformed reserved history for a channel, invalid reference roles, cross-channel refs, referenced opening missing, or inconsistent association yields unavailable. Unrelated valid historical openings whose declarations are no longer current cannot win by timestamp.

| Current observations | Evidence |
|---|---|
| No protected events for channel | legacy |
| Protected history exists but no live exact attachment/legacy association | unavailable (reason states missing/mismatched association); does not remint |
| One exact current matching open, effective held close(s) for it | closed |
| More than one current matching open, even if timestamps differ | unavailable (ambiguous opening) |
| One exact current matching unclosed open; required history refs valid; every effective received ref held | open, detached copies of complete received operand sorted by ID |
| One matching unclosed open but any effective received ref is absent/erased/invalid | unavailable for entire operand; no partial return |
| Open effectively erased, received refs remain | unavailable (missing incarnation); never infer opening from receipt |
| Close explicitly locally erased and unique exact original attachment remains | open if all remaining checks pass; otherwise unavailable |
| New exact pool declaration/open after successful drop | only new matching incarnation can answer; old receipt set cannot substitute |

Closed is reported only for a unique exact currently attached matching opening; a successfully dropped historical channel is unavailable because no live attachment remains. Multiple historical closed openings do not require a timestamp election. Bound grant/receive/cursed-law authority remains a separate live check for later activation; this evidence API proves receive lineage, not permission to render. Imported legacy controls may deny matching evidence but never fill a protected opening hole.

## Complete naming and literal fixtures

Actual `channelName(into,prefix)` is `channel:${into}:${prefix}`. Event entity ID follows existing channel status convention `channel:${name}`. For into=`ada:journal`, prefix=`peer`, name=`channel:ada:journal:peer`, event entity ID is **`channel:channel:ada:journal:peer`**.

All string fields forbid NUL. channel, into, prefix, opened-by and opened-from are nonempty; from may be empty for existing explicit local offer behavior. This new event parser refuses an empty prefix even if a legacy channel record can carry one: such channels remain legacy/unavailable for protected evidence, while ordinary root channel behavior remains unchanged. Bound opened-by equals exact binding.container and opened-from equals exact binding.inbox at issuance. nonce is lowercase hex length exactly 64 from `globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32))` with lowercase hex encoding, preserving the existing browser bundle and adding no Node-only import, not time-derived.

Complete open literal (A/B are real complete fixture status/declaration delta addresses; author OP is fixture operator):

```json
{"timestamp":100,"author":"OP","pointers":[
 {"role":"event","target":{"kind":"entity","entity":{"id":"channel:channel:ada:journal:peer","context":"loam.local.channel.event"}}},
 {"role":"version","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":1}},
 {"role":"action","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"open"}},
 {"role":"nonce","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}},
 {"role":"into","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"ada:journal"}},
 {"role":"prefix","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"peer"}},
 {"role":"from","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"https://peer.example/default"}},
 {"role":"opener-kind","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"bound"}},
 {"role":"opened-by","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"ada:journal"}},
 {"role":"opened-from","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"inbox:ada:journal:CONNECTION_KEY"}},
 {"role":"status-at-open","target":{"kind":"delta","deltaRef":{"delta":"A"}}},
 {"role":"pool-declaration","target":{"kind":"delta","deltaRef":{"delta":"B"}}}
]}
```

Complete close literal (O is real signed open fixture ID):

```json
{"timestamp":102,"author":"OP","pointers":[
 {"role":"event","target":{"kind":"entity","entity":{"id":"channel:channel:ada:journal:peer","context":"loam.local.channel.event"}}},
 {"role":"version","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":1}},
 {"role":"action","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"close"}},
 {"role":"opening","target":{"kind":"delta","deltaRef":{"delta":"O"}}},
 {"role":"reason","target":{"kind":"primitive","value":"drop"}}
]}
```

The received literal earlier uses the same actual event entity ID convention (replace its illustrative short entity with this full name for these fixtures). All returned opening objects and received arrays/claims are detached immutable copies.

## Named verification paths

Acceptance criteria 1–7 and 9: new `test/federation/local-channel-events.test.ts`; real local/channel gateway fixtures plus deterministic backend and ingestVia seams. Criterion 8: same new file for protected controls/erase cases, with existing `test/gateway/erase.test.ts`, `test/gateway/erase-tier-completeness.test.ts` and `test/gateway/erase-inmemory-reach.test.ts` as compatibility control, not a claimed authored file. Extend new-file cases to cover unknown-target preplants, batch forward negation closure, failed-purge tombstone forgiveness attempts, erased received-strike revival after explicit local erase, actual rejected/throwing ingest, concurrent fresh opens, stale rejected pull and drop/scheduler deadlock. Relevant existing `test/federation/channel-open.test.ts`, `channel-subscribe.test.ts`, `standing-sync.test.ts` and `test/federation/arrival-attestations.test.ts`, `test/federation/crash-window.test.ts` must retain root behavior. Literal parser fixtures cannot be generated solely by production builders.

A fresh legacy-compatible open whose fields cannot satisfy the strict protected schema (for example an existing allowed empty prefix) completes as legacy, with no protected event; do not change its root return behavior or report it as protected. Required bound workflows must use a representable exact prefix.


Additional verification of the existing drop contract: unavailable received source bytes do not invalidate an otherwise exact legitimate opening or prevent its authorized close and cleanup. Drop needs lifecycle identity, not a complete usable received operand. Malformed/ambiguous opening authority is not waived. Add test/federation/local-channel-drop-erased-source.test.ts with real received source erasure followed by drop, close-before-purge ordering and an independent live bystander. Preserve the original frozen rail. Author and measure the additional regression before fixing the source; freeze it through the ticket service and Git. This separates cleanup identity from read eligibility without widening erasure reach.

Additional verification of exact fresh declaration capture: test/federation/local-channel-opening-race.test.ts must hold a real asynchronous opening boundary and insert another same-name declaration. The local opening cannot substitute that later declaration for the exact delta authored by its own creation. Capture the authored ID before awaits; revalidate current attachment and refuse protected success if the exact association changed. Existing legacy partial-state failure behavior remains honest. This verifies the already-normative exact-reference rule, without granting new import authority. Author and measure the regression before its source fix, then freeze through the service and Git. Preserve all earlier rails.

Verified P5 resume regressions require additional independent controls in test/federation/local-channel-resume-incarnation.test.ts. A handle resumed while its exact valid opening is closed retains that incarnation; after explicit local erase(close) revives it, synchronization must work without another restart. It remains unable to sync while closed. Both resume paths follow this rule. Legacy handles also retain their exact attachment and declaration, even when they have no protected opening: old fresh/resumed handles cannot sync a replacement legacy channel with identical name/source/opener fields. Refuse stale success and stale failure before debt/status/source/receipt writes. These controls verify the original lifecycle and replay promises; no new authority, promotion of legacy history, or broader deletion follows. Freeze measured regressions before source fixes.

Receipt service boundary addendum: issueChannelEvent permits only open/close, with runtime refusal of caller-supplied received actions. A module-private received writer is reachable through an internal receiveChannelOfferInCommit(gw, exactOpening, offeredDeltas) operation that resolves the actual current pool itself and performs actual pool.federate admission. It takes no arbitrary received IDs, reports, pool, persistence callback or admission callback. Preserve the existing outer per-name channel queue across receive and bookkeeping; this internal already-in-commit cross-module primitive does not reacquire the queue or claim to authenticate trusted host lock ownership. Copy the association and offer before awaits, revalidate exact current association, and derive new receipt members only from actual admittedIds minus already-attested IDs. Preserve source-before-receipt persistence, actual pool.federate fault wrappers, report/debt/arrival failure behavior, quiet polls and delta-only replay. An explicit result may carry the successful source report plus a receipt-stage failure; it is not durable authority. The existing raw backend/trusted host boundary remains. See independent T288-receipt-boundary-premortem.md and verdict for executable failure controls. Additional independent regressions in test/federation/local-channel-receive-boundary.test.ts must be frozen before source repair; all previous rails remain unchanged.
title: Record protected local channel incarnations and validated receive events
